clinical_category: Total knee arthroplasty - functional discharge readiness and rehabilitation coordination
blueprint_topic: Discharge planning, interdisciplinary referral, and continuity of care
stem: A client is scheduled for discharge home after total knee replacement but still requires hands-on help to transfer and cannot safely walk with the prescribed walker or manage the stairs needed to enter the home. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Communicate that the current discharge plan may be unsafe and coordinate reassessment with physical therapy and the discharge/case-management team to determine additional training, support, or a different discharge setting.
options.B: Discharge the client as planned because postoperative mobility goals do not affect readiness for home care.
options.C: Tell the client to practice the stairs alone after arriving home because rehabilitation should begin only after hospital discharge.
options.D: Cancel all future physical therapy because needing assistance before discharge indicates that rehabilitation is unlikely to help.

rationale: A is correct. AAOS patient guidance after total knee replacement includes functional discharge goals such as safe transfers, ambulation with an appropriate assistive device, and stair negotiation when stairs are part of the discharge environment. AAOS also notes that if these goals cannot be achieved or adequate help is unavailable, direct discharge home may be unsafe and temporary rehabilitation or skilled-nursing care may be needed. NCSBN places discharge planning, referrals, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continuity of care within Management of Care. B ignores functional safety. C sends an unready client into an avoidable fall-risk situation. D is incorrect because physical therapy is part of restoring mobility and function; failure to meet goals indicates a need for additional assessment/support, not abandonment of rehabilitation. The final item tests the nurse's role in coordinating a safe discharge rather than simply recalling that physical therapy is beneficial.
educational_objective: Recognize when postoperative mobility deficits make a planned home discharge unsafe and coordinate physical-therapy and discharge-planning reassessment to establish an appropriate level of support or care setting.
source_organization: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Activities After Total Knee Replacement; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: Current AAOS OrthoInfo resource accessed 2026-08-18; NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: AAOS OrthoInfo 'Activities After Total Knee Replacement' → discharge-readiness section: goals include getting in/out of bed, acceptable pain control, walking with an assistive device, managing required stairs and performing prescribed exercises; if these goals are not met or adequate home help is unavailable, direct home discharge may be unsafe and transfer to rehabilitation/skilled nursing may be considered. NCSBN 2026 Test Plan → Management of Care: discharge planning, referrals, multidisciplinary collaboration and continuity of care.
source_claim_supported: Current AAOS guidance directly supports functional mobility goals as part of discharge readiness after total knee replacement and the possibility that clients who cannot meet them need additional rehabilitation/support; NCSBN supports nursing coordination of discharge and referrals.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care: coordinate discharge planning, assess need for referrals, collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, update the plan of care and promote continuity of care.
correction_summary: Total quality rebuild. The source was a low-discrimination statement that physical therapy supports recovery. The final item turns this into a concrete Management-of-Care decision about unsafe functional discharge readiness, using AAOS criteria and NCSBN care-coordination responsibilities. It is distinct from V2-Q1850, which addressed conflicting multidisciplinary instructions rather than failure to meet mobility goals.
audit_findings: The original item only described the value of physical therapy and did not test a meaningful nursing decision.
Fresh AAOS review gives concrete functional discharge goals after total knee replacement and states that direct home discharge can be unsafe when they are not met.
NCSBN independently supports multidisciplinary discharge planning and referrals within Management of Care.
Distractors test discharge despite unsafe mobility, unsupervised home stair practice and abandonment of rehabilitation; none is defensible.
